mainTopic: Firewood on יום טוב: gathered vs. scattered wood, what counts as a קרפף, and limits on chopping wood
overview: The משנה rules that on יום טוב you may bring firewood from an open field only if it was gathered into a pile, but from a קרפף (an enclosed storage yard) you may bring even scattered wood. רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about what counts as a קרפף. In the גמרא, שמואל is stricter: only wood that is both gathered and inside a קרפף may be brought. The גמרא explains that our משנה follows a lone opinion, the version of the בית שמאי–בית הלל argument reported by רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. רבא adds that light leaves count as scattered even in a pile, unless a vessel was placed on them before יום טוב. The גמרא then asks how to read the קרפף dispute and proves from רבי יוסי's wording that he is lenient twice: a place near the city counts even without a lock, and a locked place counts even far away, as long as it is within the תחום. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, to be lenient. A new משנה begins: wood may not be chopped from building beams on יום טוב, and chopping may be done only with a cleaver, not with weekday tools.

steps.title: Which firewood may be brought on the holiday
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits bringing gathered wood from a field, and even scattered wood from a קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: You may bring wood from the field, but only from wood that was gathered into a pile. From a קרפף, you may bring even scattered wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us where a person may take firewood from on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood lying loose in an open field is treated as מוקצה, because the owner did not have it in mind for use. Once it is gathered into a pile, it is ready for use. A קרפף is an enclosed, guarded yard, so even loose wood there stays in the owner's mind and may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: An enclosed yard used for storage
Set aside from use, so it may not be handled on שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: In a field only gathered wood is allowed. In a קרפף even scattered wood is allowed. The location changes the rule.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One may bring wood from the field —
from that which is gathered,
phrases.notes: Only wood piled up before יום טוב

phrases.english: and from the karpef — even from the scattered.
phrases.notes: The enclosure keeps the wood in the owner's mind

steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a field, only gathered wood may be brought. In a קרפף, even scattered wood may be brought.

steps.title: Defining what counts as a קרפף
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a קרפף is any enclosure near the city. רבי יוסי says it is any enclosure entered with a key, as long as it is within the תחום שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a קרפף? Any enclosure close to the city. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: any place you enter with a key, even if it is far away, as long as it is within the תחום שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines the word קרפף, since the lenient rule depends on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, closeness to the city is what makes a place guarded. For רבי יוסי, a locked entrance is enough, even far from the city, as long as the place is within the תחום שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The distance limit (2,000 אמות) one may walk outside the town

phrases.english: What is a karpef? —

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁסָּמוּךְ לְעִיר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: Any that is near the city; these are the words of Rabbi Yehudah.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל שֶׁנִּכְנָסִין לוֹ בְּפוֹתַחַת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: any that one enters with a key,
even if it is only within the Shabbat limit.
phrases.notes: It may be far from the city, but it must be inside the תחום

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines a key term from the ruling in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a קרפף is near the city. רבי יוסי: a קרפף is any locked enclosure within the תחום.

steps.title: שמואל allows only wood that is both gathered and in a קרפף
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that firewood may be brought only if it is gathered and inside a קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: You may only bring wood that is gathered and inside a קרפף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from שמואל that is stricter than the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל requires two conditions together: the wood must be gathered, and it must be in a קרפף. That means no wood at all from a field, and no scattered wood even in a קרפף. Both are things the משנה allowed.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehudah said that Shmuel said:
One may not bring wood
except from the gathered wood that is in the karpef.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter rule than the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only wood that is both gathered and in a קרפף may be brought.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה that permits scattered wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה explicitly allows scattered wood in a קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: from a קרפף, even scattered wood may be brought!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל by quoting the משנה, which directly contradicts him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל forbids scattered wood even in a קרפף, but the משנה says out loud that it is permitted. An אמורא like שמואל is not supposed to argue with a משנה, so this is a strong attack.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in the משנה)? The opening of a challenge

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
from the karpef — even from the scattered!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that scattered wood in a קרפף is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly permits scattered wood in a קרפף, which directly contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: The משנה follows a lone opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our משנה reflects a single, minority view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is the view of one individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by saying the משנה follows a minority opinion, so שמואל may rule like the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל is not arguing with the משנה on his own. The משנה follows one תנא who is outnumbered, and שמואל rules like the majority of תנאים. The next step brings the source showing who that lone opinion is.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the משנה is a mistake. It means the משנה records a real תנא's view, which happens to be the minority one.

phrases.english: Our mishnah is an individual opinion.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a minority view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is the accepted ruling, so שמואל contradicts it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows a minority view, and שמואל follows the majority.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version of the בית שמאי–בית הלל argument
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reports a lenient בית הלל matching our משנה, which identifies the lone opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said, בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about scattered wood in fields, which may not be brought. They also did not argue about gathered wood in a קרפף, which may be brought. What did they argue about? Scattered wood in a קרפף and gathered wood in fields. בית שמאי say: he may not bring it. בית הלל say: he may bring it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the lenient view in our משנה belongs to one תנא, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version, בית הלל permit exactly what our משנה permits: gathered wood in a field and scattered wood in a קרפף. Since this is his own report against the other חכמים, the majority must hold that even בית הלל allow only gathered wood in a קרפף. That is exactly שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
The two great schools of תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version of בית הלל. The majority of חכמים, and שמואל with them, allow only wood that is both gathered and in a קרפף.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how שמואל can rule against our משנה: the משנה follows a lone view, and he follows the majority.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about scattered wood in the fields, that one may not bring it,
nor about gathered wood in the karpef, that one may bring it.
About what did they disagree? —
about scattered wood in the karpef
and about gathered wood in the fields,
for Beit Shammai say: he may not bring it,
and Beit Hillel say: he may bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.raayaObject: The claim that our משנה is a minority view
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר

steps.title: Light leaves count as scattered even when piled
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that reed and vine leaves count as scattered, even in a pile, because the wind can blow them away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Reed leaves and vine leaves, even though people gather them and set them down in one place, count as scattered and are forbidden, because if a wind comes it will scatter them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new rule about what counts as "gathered" for very light material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pile normally shows that the owner plans to use the material. But light leaves can blow away at any moment, so the owner does not really count on them. They are therefore treated like scattered wood and are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: עֲלֵי קָנִים וַעֲלֵי גְפָנִים,
phrases.english: Rava said: reed leaves and vine leaves,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּמְכַנְּפִי לְהוּ וּמוֹתְבִי,
phrases.english: even though they gather them and set them down,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִי מִדְּלֵי זִיקָא מְבַדַּר לְהוּ —
phrases.english: since if a wind rises it scatters them —
they are like scattered wood and are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: עֲלֵי קָנִים וַעֲלֵי גְפָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the gathered/scattered rule to light material
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Piled leaves that the wind can scatter count as scattered and are forbidden.

steps.title: A vessel placed on the leaves makes them permitted
steps.stepSummary: If a vessel was placed on the leaves before יום טוב, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if someone placed a vessel on them the day before, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds an exception: weighing the leaves down before יום טוב makes them count as truly gathered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessel stops the wind from scattering the leaves. Doing this before יום טוב shows that the owner planned to use them. So they become prepared, not מוקצה.
steps.whatToRemember: Firewood must be truly gathered. Light leaves count as gathered only if something holds them down from before יום טוב.

phrases.english: But if one placed a vessel on them from the day before —
it is fine.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaves weighed down by a vessel before יום טוב are permitted.

steps.title: How should the קרפף dispute be read? First possibility
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to read the משנה about a קרפף. The first option is that רבי יהודה requires both nearness to the city and a lock, and רבי יוסי only relaxes the distance.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the משנה's line 'What is a קרפף': a question was asked. What exactly does it mean? Perhaps רבי יהודה means a place near the city, but only if it has a lock. Then רבי יוסי comes to say that since it has a lock, it counts even if it is only within the תחום שבת (and not right next to the city).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a question about the משנה and lays out the first possible way to read the dispute. The second way comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, both תנאים require a lock. They argue only about distance: רבי יהודה says 'near the city,' and רבי יוסי says 'anywhere within the תחום.' This makes רבי יוסי simply more lenient than רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: An enclosed storage yard outside the house. Wood stored there is not מוקצה on יום טוב.
'It was asked of them.' This opens a real question the גמרא wants to resolve.
A key or lock: the enclosure is locked and entered with a key.
The 2,000-אמה zone around a city that one may walk within on שבת or יום טוב.

phrases.english: 'What is a karpef' etc.
A question was raised before them:
How is it saying it?
'Any place that is near the city'
provided that it has a lock,
and Rabbi Yosei comes to say:
since it has a lock,
even if it is merely within the Shabbat limit, it also counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבא's rulings about leaves to a new question on the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה require a lock as well as nearness? Is רבי יוסי only adding leniency?

steps.title: Second possibility: רבי יוסי is lenient on distance but strict about the lock
steps.stepSummary: The other option is that רבי יהודה requires only nearness, with or without a lock. רבי יוסי allows any place within the תחום, but only if it is locked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe this is what it means. רבי יהודה says any place near the city counts, whether or not it has a lock. Then רבי יוסי comes to say that even a place within the תחום שבת counts, but only if it has a lock. Without a lock, it does not count even if it is near the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the question. The next step will decide between the two readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the two תנאים each have one leniency and one stringency. רבי יהודה is stricter about distance but does not need a lock. רבי יוסי is looser about distance but insists on a lock. So a near-the-city enclosure with no lock would be fine for רבי יהודה and forbidden for רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or perhaps.' This introduces the second side of a question.
'Whether... or...' The rule applies in both cases.

phrases.english: Or perhaps this is what it is saying:
any place that is near the city
whether it has a lock
or does not have a lock,
and Rabbi Yosei comes to say:
even within the Shabbat limit,
but only specifically if it has a lock,
but if it does not have a lock,
even near the city it does not count.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume רבי יוסי must be the lenient one across the board. In this second reading he is actually stricter than רבי יהודה in one case: a place near the city with no lock.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question opened in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי יוסי's lock requirement a new stringency that רבי יהודה does not share?

steps.title: The wording of רבי יוסי shows he is lenient in both ways
steps.stepSummary: From the way רבי יוסי's words are phrased, the גמרא proves that he only adds leniency. He is lenient on both counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear. The משנה says: רבי יוסי says, 'Any place that one enters with a key, and even within the תחום שבת.' Learn from this that רבי יוסי is stating two leniencies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by looking closely at רבי יוסי's exact words in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי phrases his view as an addition: 'any place entered with a key, and EVEN within the תחום.' He does not phrase it as a condition, as if to say 'only if it has a key.' So he is not cutting back on what רבי יהודה allowed. He is lenient twice: an enclosure near the city counts even without a lock, and a locked enclosure counts even far from the city, as long as it is within the תחום. He is never stricter than רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear.' This introduces a proof from a source.
'From the fact that it teaches.' The proof comes from the exact wording.
'Two leniencies.' He is lenient on two points.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
since it teaches: Rabbi Yosei says:
'Any place one enters with a key,'
'and even within the Shabbat limit,'
learn from this that Rabbi Yosei
is stating two leniencies.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִדְּקָתָנֵי, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question raised in steps 9 and 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי's words ('כל... ואפילו') only add cases, so he never adds a stringency. He is lenient in both ways.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of רבי יוסי in the משנה itself.

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms: yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one pushes back on the proof. So it is settled: רבי יוסי is lenient on both counts and never stricter than רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Learn from it.' Here it means the proof stands and the point is accepted.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי states two leniencies. A place near the city counts even without a key, and a locked place counts even far away, as long as it is within the תחום.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, to be lenient
steps.stepSummary: רב סלא, quoting רבי ירמיה, rules like רבי יוסי as a leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סלא said in the name of רבי ירמיה: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we understand רבי יוסי's view, an אמורא gives the practical ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'to be lenient' match what was just proven. In practice, an enclosure counts as a קרפף in either case: if it is near the city, even without a key, or if it is locked and within the תחום שבת, even far from the city.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The halacha follows...' This is the practical ruling.

steps.whatToRemember: A קרפף counts if it is near the city (even with no lock), or if it is locked and within the תחום. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי's double leniency.
steps.whyThisMatters: This decides in practice which stored wood is not מוקצה on יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rav Salla said in the name of Rabbi Yirmeya:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yosei, to be lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְהָקֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling based on the reading that was just proven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי as a leniency.

steps.title: New משנה: limits on chopping wood on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה says that on יום טוב one may not chop wood from building beams, even a beam that broke on יום טוב. Regular woodcutting tools are also forbidden. Only a cleaver is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: On יום טוב one may not chop wood from beams, and not from a beam that broke on יום טוב. And one may not chop with an axe, a saw, or a sickle. One may chop only with a cleaver.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives two rules about chopping firewood on יום טוב: which wood is allowed and which tool is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building beams are set aside for construction, so they are מוקצה. A beam that broke on יום טוב was still מוקצה when the day began, so it stays forbidden. Axes, saws, and sickles are ordinary weekday tools. Chopping with them looks too much like a weekday job. A cleaver is a kitchen tool, so using it is a clear change from the usual way of chopping.

keyTerms.meaning: A cleaver: a heavy kitchen knife for cutting meat.

steps.confusionAlert: Even a beam that broke on יום טוב, and is now useless for building, is still forbidden. What matters is its status when יום טוב began.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may not chop wood
neither from the beams

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִן הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: nor from a beam that broke on the Festival.
And one may not chop, neither with an axe,
nor with a saw, nor with a sickle,
but only with a cleaver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the קרפף discussion has been concluded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood may not be chopped from beams, even a beam that broke on יום טוב. Chopping may be done only with a cleaver, not with an axe, saw, or sickle.
